name: Clariane SE
reason: Leveraged nursing-home operator: adjusted EPS fell from EUR 0.88 (2018) to EUR 0.23 (2025), EBIT margin is 5.6% vs a 10.4% peak, net debt/EBITDA is 6.9x and shares grew 10%/yr through rescue equity raises.

name: Wizz Air Holdings Plc
reason: Low-cost airline with commodity economics: adjusted EPS went from EUR 2.72 (FY2019) to EUR 0.03, EBIT margin is -2.0% (10y avg -2.5%), net debt/EBITDA is 4.8x and consensus FY1 EPS is a loss.

name: Icade SA
reason: French office REIT in structural decline: FFO/share fell from EUR 4.61 (2022) to EUR 3.34 (2025), consensus sees -12.6% FY1 and negative LTG, and net debt/EBITDA is 12.0x.

name: Autoneum Holding AG
reason: Auto-parts supplier with no pricing power: adjusted EPS of CHF 10.32 (2025) is below CHF 18.47 (2017), 10y EBIT margin averages 4.6% and ROIC 4.9%, and growth tracks global vehicle production.

name: CECONOMY AG
reason: Electronics retailer (MediaMarkt/Saturn) with a 10y average EBIT margin of 0.6%, adjusted EPS down from EUR 0.60 (FY2016) to EUR 0.06 and ROIC of 2.1%: cheap but ordinary with online-competition pressure.

name: Energean Plc
reason: Gas E&P whose earnings are set by commodity prices and Israeli gas contracts: adjusted EPS swung from USD 1.05 (2023) to a USD -1.40 loss (2025), with net debt/EBITDA of 3.0x and geopolitical concentration in Israel.

name: Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA
reason: Airline rebuilt after restructuring with shares compounding 95%/yr over 10y; EBIT margin of 8.8% sits at the 91st pctile of a history averaging -14.1%, so earnings are at a cyclical high in a commodity industry.

name: Lagardere SA
reason: Travel retail plus publishing conglomerate with adjusted EPS only EUR 1.83 (2015) to EUR 2.26 (2025, ~2%/yr), EBIT margin at a 10y high of 7.1%, net debt/EBITDA 3.0x and a low free float under Louis Hachette Group.

name: Global Ship Lease, Inc.
reason: Containership lessor whose EPS of USD 10.26 (2025) is at its 10y peak after the post-Covid charter boom; consensus sees -8.5% and -8.7% in FY2/FY3 as charters roll, and share count grew 18%/yr over 10y.

name: Forvia SE
reason: Auto-parts supplier levered by the HELLA acquisition (acquisitions 1.7x 10y FCF, net debt/EBITDA 2.7x) with adjusted EPS falling from EUR 4.63 (2018) to a EUR -7.05 loss in 2025.

name: Volkswagen AG
reason: Mass-market automaker facing EV and Chinese competition: adjusted EPS fell from EUR 31.92 (2023) to EUR 13.29 (2025), EBIT margin is 5.3% and 10y FCF conversion is -0.31x, so the 3.6x P/E reflects ordinary economics.

name: Philogen SpA
reason: Clinical-stage oncology biotech whose 2025 EPS of EUR 5.70 (80% EBIT margin) came from licensing income after years of losses; consensus sees -88.6% in FY1, so earnings depend on binary pipeline and regulatory outcomes.

name: GN Store Nord A/S
reason: Hearing aids are a good oligopoly, but the group is diluted by consumer gaming and enterprise headsets: adjusted EPS fell from DKK 13.49 (2021) to DKK 4.39 after the SteelSeries deal (acquisitions 1.3x 10y FCF) and net debt/EBITDA is 3.2x.

name: Clarivate PLC
reason: Roll-up of information services (acquisitions 3.9x 10y FCF) with net debt/EBITDA of 4.4x, a 10y average ROIC of -8.0% and adjusted EPS down from USD 0.85 (2022) to USD 0.69, plus AI disruption risk to its content and analytics.

name: Emeis
reason: The former Orpea, restructured after a scandal with massive dilution (shares +67%/yr over 10y): adjusted EPS is still negative (EUR -1.34 in 2025), net debt/EBITDA is 10.4x and EBIT margin is 2.0%.

name: BlueNord ASA
reason: North Sea oil and gas producer (Tyra) with earnings set by commodity prices and field ramp-ups: adjusted EPS went from USD -1.77 (2024) to USD 3.03 (2025), and consensus sees FY3 at -17%.

name: Nexa Resources S.A.
reason: Zinc miner and smelter in Peru and Brazil whose earnings follow metal prices: adjusted EPS has had 0 of 4 years of ≥7% growth and swung between USD -1.19 (2024) and USD 1.00 (2025), with a 10y average ROIC of -2.0%.

name: ProSiebenSat.1 Media SE
reason: Linear TV broadcaster in structural decline: adjusted EPS fell from EUR 2.40 (2017) to EUR 0.68 (2025), EBIT margin went from 22.2% to 5.8%, and it is now controlled by MFE.

name: Neinor Homes SA
reason: Spanish homebuilder whose earnings follow the housing cycle: adjusted EPS of EUR 0.87 (2025) is below EUR 1.17 (2023), net debt/EBITDA is 9.4x and the business has no structural moat.

name: Philip Morris CR as
reason: Cigarette maker controlled by PMI with secular volume decline and Czech excise pressure: EPS fell from CZK 1,464 (2019) to CZK 1,106 (2025) and EBIT margin fell from 35.8% to 17.0%, so there is no route to ≥7% growth despite high ROIC.
